<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **41** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_
- `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`  _(via nav_home (literal, a string literal in validateAppNavigationPresent))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via validateWidgetBindings (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 49 pages)`, `objectName (literal, 60 pages)`
- **18** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `324c21475f5a8b58f675642d08d9ed28735fb03b` — the merge of head `2399eab8c8d4def0a51a605fe5d08fa920893bee` into base `581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 324c21475f5a8b58f675642d08d9ed28735fb03b && git checkout 324c21475f5a8b58f675642d08d9ed28735fb03b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194 2399eab8c8d4def0a51a605fe5d08fa920893bee && git checkout -B drift-repro 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194 && git merge --no-ff 2399eab8c8d4def0a51a605fe5d08fa920893bee

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

First round on this PR. Face: the file list (17 paths) holds one published-schema path (the ADR-0087 entry, first on the Scope line), and the PR body and the changeset both declare `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces, twelve files. Inputs: card #35143, the claim 7230739921, the report 7232386063, the PR body, the net diff against main at `93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042` (the head's second parent), the contract reviews on #37513 and #37807 of the same card, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run; every statement about a test below is a reading of the test and of the code it drives.

### ① Derived judgments

- `list-view-filter-field-virtual` (error; CLI, the `view` and `object` doors): RIGHT.
  - The engine refuses every `where` that names a `formula` field with `400 INVALID_FIELD`, at the REST ingress and at the engine seam (`assertFilterIsMaterializable`, `filter-comparand-shape.ts:462`, called from `engine-top-level.ts:937` and `:1069`; the ledger entry `engine-find-formula-filter-refused` of protocol 17 states both doors).
  - The rule asks the predicate the engine asks (`isVirtualSearchField`, whose set is `formula` and nothing else), so `summary` and `autonumber`, which have columns, are not refused.
  - A list view with no resolvable object, a dotted key and an unreadable type are not judged. A filter that reaches no store is not reached by the rule.
  - Publish now refuses a view main accepted. That view already opened on the engine's error for every reader, so the refusal takes away nothing that worked.
- `list-view-kanban-group-field-uncategorical` (warning; CLI, `view` and `object` doors): RIGHT as an advisory. Select, radio, boolean and single-valued reference fields are silent; nothing is refused.
- `dashboard-without-widgets` (error on the CLI, warning at the `dashboard` door): WRONG on the CLI. See M1.
  - At the door a warning is right: the spec's own create seed (`metadata-create-seeds.ts:41-45`) and two Studio paths save `widgets: []`.
  - The signal for the split (`ctx.runtimeWriteType !== undefined`) is the one the reference-integrity suite already reads. That part is sound.
- `app-navigation-empty` (warning; CLI and the `app` door): RIGHT as an advisory. A separator and an empty group count as nothing; areas and the stack's own contributions count.
- `object-unreachable-from-navigation` and `object-without-view` (warnings, CLI only): the registration is right (`CLI_ONLY`, full snapshot). What they report is S2, S3 and M2.
  - The per-package pass hands sibling packages along (`packageBodyAsStack(pkg.body, artifactPackageEntries)`), so navigation one package contributes into another's app does count there.
- Public surface: WIDENED. `packages/lint/src/index.ts` adds six rule-id constants on `.`, and the exported `validateWidgetBindings` gains a second parameter whose type (`WidgetBindingOptions`) is reachable through it.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: WRONG at this head. See S1.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: RIGHT. A value an author could publish (a list filter keyed on a formula) is refused.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch: right for this diff. Minor covers the narrowing and the added exports; the spec adds only the upgrade-guide entry. No `major`.
- The title carries `!`. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, two FROM and TO pairs, both declaration lines and one marker, `adr-0087: registered publish-refuses-views-and-dashboards-that-save-and-do-not-work`. The entry's id and file name match the marker.
- The entry and the changeset describe the head as built. Both name the dashboard as a CLI error and move with M1.
- A fix of M1 that edits `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` adds `@objectstack/cli` at patch.
- The dogfood battery is reported at `f23263ca` (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, 490 files passed, 3 skipped), one merge of main behind this head. It is owed on the head that closes M1.
- Docs counts, a prose face, read because asked: main holds 87 registry rules (#37971 landed), this head holds 89, and the four count lines say 89.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The head is a merge of main (`93fa9118`) into `f23263ca`, the head this review was read at. The merge is confirmed to carry nothing of its own beyond the count lines:
  - the hand resolution (`git show --remerge-diff`) is four lines, "author-time rules (88)" against main's 87 resolved to 89, one in each of `cli.mdx`, `validating-metadata.mdx`, `build-with-claude-code.mdx` and `react-pages.mdx`;
  - the PR's own change under `packages/lint` and `packages/spec` has the same patch id before and after the merge, and the head differs from main in the same seventeen files;
  - what moved under `packages/lint`, `packages/spec`, `packages/cli` and `examples` between the two heads has the patch id of what main brought.
- Main brought edits to `generate.ts` and the showcase. Neither touches a finding below: `generate.ts:720` still writes `widgets: []`, the showcase list holds no entry for the new rules, and its app navigation still names none of the five objects of M2.
- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-28T02:35Z: 37 runs, 7 success, 9 skipped, 21 in progress, none failed. "All green" is not established. The previous head had no run at all (it did not merge), so no CI result exists for this diff yet.
  - The report lists the lint, metadata-protocol, objectql, runtime and dogfood suites. It lists no `@objectstack/cli` suite and marks `app-showcase` NOT MEASURED. M1 and M2 sit in exactly those two.
- Open question 1 (the Clause-② spelling): neither A nor B. The gate does refuse a bare `no` beside `narrowed`, and the line it wants here is `yes (narrowing)`, as #37807 landed. S1.
- Open question 2 (the dashboard split): B, a warning at both doors. M1 gives the reasons.
- File surface: the claim names `packages/lint/**`, the docs table, generated pages and one changeset. The diff also adds `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.…ts`. The PR body admits it; the seat's scope line is still to write, as on #37513 and #37807. Closing M1 or M2 reaches `packages/cli/**` and `examples/app-showcase/**`, which the seat has to admit first.
- `Skills-docs:` reads "follow-up owed" and names two skill files but no card. #37513 and #37807 named a card number on that line.
- `Security-touching: no`. The one security-named file in the diff is a test whose rule roster for an `app` write gains the new advisory; no hunk changes or teaches a permission, sharing or credential behaviour.
- SQL push-down: the diff reads metadata only and issues no query. Nothing to report.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — `dashboard-without-widgets` as a CLI error refuses what the CLI itself writes, and reds two suites main pins.
- `os generate dashboard NAME` writes `widgets: []` (`packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts:720`, under the comment "While this is empty the dashboard has nothing to draw").
- Main pins that scaffold as passing every gate:
  - `generate-scaffolds-reach-stack.e2e.test.ts` (#20215): `os init -t app`, `os g` every type, then `os validate` exits 0.
  - `generate-scaffold-gates.e2e.test.ts` (#21325, #32153): after `os g dashboard`, `validate`, `build` and `lint` each exit 0 with `findings` equal to `[]`, and the starter ledger is pinned empty.
- At this head the registry entry runs on all three commands and returns an error for that file. By reading, both suites fail. Neither was run by the dev, and CI had not answered when this was read.
- The reason given for the door (the platform's own create step writes the empty shape and fills it afterwards) holds for the CLI in the same words. "In a shipped source tree an empty dashboard is never the intent" does not hold for a tree someone is still building, and `os validate` and `os build` are run on those.
- This is not the split #37807 settled. There the two doors knew different things (one stack against the whole served collection), and severity followed what each could decide. Here both doors see the whole dashboard and know the same fact. Only a guess about intent differs.
- The shape also breaks no request: the dashboard opens on its header. The same PR grades the same class (`app-navigation-empty`, an app that opens on an empty state, saved empty by Studio first) as a warning at both doors.
- Closing condition, one of:
  - (a) the finding is a warning on the CLI as at the door; the changeset, the entry, the explanation and the docs row say so; and the scaffold pins are settled deliberately, since a warning still breaks the `[]` pins (the generator stops writing an empty dashboard, or the pins carry the finding with its reason);
  - (b) the error stays, the generator stops writing `widgets: []`, the pins move with it, and the PR says why an in-progress tree should fail its build.
- This reviewer's reading is (a). Under (a) the narrowing is the list filter alone, and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` still stands.

M2 (must-fix) — the three app-shell advisories were not measured against the suites that pin the CLI's finding set.
- `examples/app-showcase/test/author-time-advisories.test.ts` (#32168) fails on any finding not on its list. The report marks the showcase NOT MEASURED.
  - By reading, `object-unreachable-from-navigation` fires there. `src/ui/apps/index.ts` names thirteen objects in `type: 'object'` entries. `showcase_announcement`, `showcase_client_brief`, `showcase_inquiry`, `showcase_private_note` and `showcase_semantic_zoo` are not among them, and none has a `master_detail` field or `apiEnabled: false`.
- `generate-scaffold-gates.e2e.test.ts`: `os g object ticket` writes an object and adds no navigation entry (only the dashboard generator carries `navEntry`). The project has a starter app, so the new object is reported, against a pin of no finding at any severity.
- Closing condition: every check-run on the head is green, and the PR names these two suites as run. Each new finding on the showcase is either fixed in its metadata or listed with its reason, as that test requires.

S1 (should-fix) — the declaration line reads `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` while the diff enlarges a published surface.
- Same finding as S3 on #37807 (record 7211486008). The criterion is "widens the accept set or enlarges the public surface", and the surface is what the entry declarations reach (`execution-duties.md:75-77`).
- Six exports on the `.` entry and a new parameter type on an exported function meet it. The changeset's own last paragraph lists them.
- "Same as #37513" does not carry over: there the ids stayed module-local.
- It hides nothing from this review, since the narrowing and schema faces already set the tier. That is why it is not a must-fix.
- Closing condition: the PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, and the seat notes the change against the claim line of 7230739921; or the exports are withdrawn.

S2 (should-fix) — `object-without-view` names a fix the schema refuses.
- The hint, the explanation and the changeset say to declare "`list: { type: 'grid', columns: [...] }` on" the object. `ObjectSchema` has no `list` key; its list views are `listViews` (`object.zod.ts:4953`). The only `list` keys in that file are `relatedLists` entries.
- `declaresOwnView` reads `obj.list` for the same reason, a branch no parsed object reaches.
- The card asks for "a finding that names the fix". The second half of the hint (`defineView`) is right.
- Closing condition: the hint, the explanation and the changeset name `listViews`, and the dead read goes.

S3 (should-fix) — "no user can reach its list" is judged on `type: 'object'` entries alone.
- Not counted: an object a `page` entry's page lists, and a `lookup` child its parent shows through `relatedLists` (a related list is not `master_detail` only).
- The hint prescribes a `master_detail` field, which changes delete and sharing behaviour, to an object that may already be shown.
- The showcase reading under M2 is the measure: five objects of the reference app are told they are unreachable.
- It is advisory and CLI only, which is why it is not a must-fix.
- Closing condition: an object another object lists in `relatedLists` is not judged (the reason the `master_detail` exemption gives), the message claims only what was read (no navigation entry opens its list), and the corpus reading covers the showcase and hotcrm.

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1. `object-without-view` is also reported for an object whose only entry carries `recordId`, which opens a record and shows no list.
- N2. `judgedHolders` returns a one-element list through a `Holder` indirection; `viewBinds` is a second spelling of the view walk in `validate-list-view-field-refs.ts:1862-1910`.
- N3. A board grouped by `rating` or by a `formula` gets the generic "one lane per distinct value" message.
- N4. The PR body still gives its test and battery readings at `f23263ca` and says the counts go 86 to 88; the head is now a later merge and the count is 89.

Open at this head: M1, M2, S1, S2, S3. The next head owes a round by this reviewer.

Delta round by the reviewer of the FAIL at `56bd194a` (read at `f23263ca`, M1, M2, S1 to S3 open). Inputs: `git diff 56bd194a 2399eab8`, the net diff against main at `447757d051446c3826158153f48b52b5a24d1e55` (the merge base), the rework report 7234103660, the seat's claim note 7232499792, the PR body as re-patched, and the check-runs on this head. ### ① Derived judgments

  - Still running: all ten Test Core shards, Check Changeset, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, and the Lint and Type Check families. No Test UI shard had been created.
  - "All green" is not established. The report gives the previous head `d95f7a4e` as 58 success with Test Core (5/10) red on the three CLI fixtures this head edits. That red is the reason for the last commit, so the shard has to be read again here.

Nothing on the battery's path moved. By the letter the battery is not at the landing head; the seat accepts or re-runs.
- The seat's claim note 7232499792 records the Clause-② change, the severity ruling and the widened file surface (`packages/cli/test/**`, the generator, `examples/app-showcase/**`). The diff stays inside it.

### ④ Design judgment

Findings of the first record, at this head:

M1 (must-fix): closed.
